findings.title: [P1] Restrict login redirects to trusted local URLs
findings.body: When `returnUrl` contains attacker-controlled input such as `https://evil.example/` or `//evil.example/`, completing login redirects the authenticated user off-site. The previous implementation always used `/dashboard`. Permit only validated same-origin paths before calling `location.assign`.

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to application logs
findings.body: Every issued token is passed to `console.log` through `audit`. In environments that collect stdout, anyone with log access can recover and reuse an unexpired bearer credential. Log non-sensitive metadata instead.

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted same-origin paths
findings.body:
In a browser, passing an attacker-controlled absolute URL such as `https://evil.example/` makes `finishLogin` navigate the authenticated user off-site. The previous implementation always transitioned to `/dashboard`; accepting `returnUrl` without origin or protocol validation introduces an open redirect.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted local URLs
findings.body:
When `returnUrl` is user-controlled, values such as `https://evil.example` redirect authenticated users off-site; executable URL schemes may also create an XSS path. Validate the origin/scheme or allow only local paths before navigation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to audit logs
findings.body:
Every call records the raw issued token through `console.log`, exposing a bearer credential to console history and any log collection pipeline. Anyone with log access can reuse an unexpired token.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to application logs
findings.body:
Every call records the raw token through `console.log`. In environments that collect stdout, anyone or any downstream system with log access can recover a still-valid bearer token and impersonate its owner.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to approved same-origin paths
findings.body:
A `returnUrl` such as `https://attacker.example/phish` or `//attacker.example` now sends an authenticated user to an attacker-controlled site. If arbitrary schemes are accepted by the calling flow, `javascript:` URLs may also execute in the application's origin where browser policy permits.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
